summary: Scan for 2026-10-09. Two genius candidates, both 2026 Nobel laureates based in the US and both covered by accepted outlets: Francis Halzen (physics, UW–Madison) and Karl Deisseroth (medicine, Stanford). Time updated its Nobel coverage on Oct 8. No facepalm story met the rules. The best leads were too old, had only one accepted source, involved a crime with a victim, or were printer or clerical mistakes rather than voluntary acts. The search quota ran out partway through the scan, so the facepalm side is empty instead of being filled with weak stories. Rule checks: Halzen's IceCube observatory is in Antarctica, but he is the laureate and is based in Madison, so it is filed under WI. Deisseroth's prize was announced Oct 5, inside the 7-day window, and Time updated its coverage on Oct 8. No facepalm story met the standard; nothing published.

candidates.headline: UW–Madison physicist Francis Halzen wins the 2026 Nobel Prize in physics for neutrino work
Stanford's Karl Deisseroth shares the 2026 Nobel Prize in medicine for optogenetics
Seattle overpaid police employees $13.1 million after using 2020 pay rates
candidates.reason: Reported Oct 1, outside the 7-day window and the one-day reporting window. Only one accepted source was opened.

candidates.headline: Nine incorrect ballots sent to voters in Oxford, Maine
candidates.reason: State officials say a printer packaging error caused it, so it is not a voluntary or avoidable act by the subject. It is also a small administrative error.

candidates.headline: Pacifica City Council candidate arrested over vandalism of sign opposing him
candidates.reason: Alleged crime with a victim other than the perpetrator.

candidates.headline: Man gets stuck in blackberry bushes during Pierce County, WA police call
candidates.reason: Arose from a domestic harassment call, so there is a victim. The report was also outside the reporting window.

candidates.headline: Kendall County, Illinois, sends 300 wrong mail-in ballots
candidates.reason: Only a non-accepted source was found, and it appears to be a clerical error rather than a voluntary act.

candidates.headline: White House document misspells 'United States'
candidates.reason: Happened around Sept. 30, outside the 7-day window, and no accepted-publisher source was found.

candidates.headline: Glaucoma therapy may have rejuvenated eye cells in three patients
candidates.reason: Early company-presented Phase 1 data from three patients that Time hedged as 'may have.' Only one accepted source was found.

candidates.headline: 2026 Nobel Prize in chemistry awarded to Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai
Anne Carson wins 2026 Nobel Prize in literature
candidates.reason: Canadian writer, and the award is not tied to an achievement in the US.

candidates.headline: Navi Pillay wins 2026 Nobel Peace Prize
Protist from pond found to break genetic code rule
